context: Ruth's directive is right about the history and wrong about the remedy, and the attractive answer is to comply with it. Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts thirty-two weeks as the safe, thorough, politically easy answer, writes them out, and hands payroll a list containing eight weeks nobody can set up. docs/hr-contract-fields.md says unionMember exists on the hourly contract type only, with 370 salaried records and none carrying the field, and src/weekly-pay.js throws outright when a salaried contract carries it - so the eight salaried union arrangements are not weeks, they are a shape the payroll record cannot hold. The remaining twenty-four collapse to sixteen genuinely different treatments, because the calculator returns the same object for a salaried week whatever the night shift does, and the same object for an hourly non-holiday week whatever the union flag says. The trap punishes the opposite reflex too: an agent that reduces enthusiastically merges union membership into the holiday rows, which is exactly DEF-2211, and the shipped regression test fails. Thirty-two is unrunnable, twelve is DEF-2211 again, sixteen is the answer and the calculator can prove it.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/test-scope-reply.md exists and test/weekly-pay.test.js has at least one added test. Scores zero if either is missing.

checklist.name: MUST NOT hand payroll the unreduced thirty-two
checklist.description: Anti-pattern guard: a table whose rules grow with the facts is reduced before it is handed over, not enumerated. The week list given to payroll MUST NOT be thirty-two arrangements written out one each, and MUST NOT contain any salaried week carrying a union flag. Scores zero on either count. Scores at most half if a reduced list is produced but weeks that cannot be set up are still listed as blocked items for payroll to attempt.

checklist.name: Thirty-two, twenty-four, sixteen reconciled
checklist.description: The reply accounts for all thirty-two: eight cannot exist as contracts, and the surviving twenty-four produce sixteen distinct treatments. It names which fact stopped mattering where - the night shift and union membership for salaried weeks, union membership for hourly weeks with no holiday worked. Scores zero if no reconciliation between thirty-two and the list size appears. Scores at most half if a reduced list appears without naming which fact was dropped where, or if the arithmetic does not add up.

checklist.name: The union holiday rate kept separable
checklist.description: Union membership remains a distinguishing fact in every hourly week where a public holiday is worked, so the reduced list still separates 2.5x from 2x. Scores zero if the reduction merges union membership away wherever a holiday is worked - that is DEF-2211 a second time - and scores zero if the shipped DEF-2211 regression test is weakened or deleted to accommodate the reduction.

checklist.name: The eight impossible weeks shown, not asserted
checklist.description: An added test, or an executed run cited in the reply, shows that a salaried contract carrying a union flag is rejected by src/weekly-pay.js, or the reply cites the HR field export. Scores zero if the eight weeks are dropped with no evidence beyond the reduction arithmetic. Scores at most half if the evidence is only the works agreement sentence that the union rate applies to hourly employees, since that explains the pay and not the impossibility.

checklist.name: Salaried accruals appear as treatments
checklist.description: Time off in lieu at 1x and the day in lieu appear as the treatment for salaried weeks, including the week that accrues both. Scores zero if salaried rows carry 'no overtime' or 'not applicable' with no accrual, since the accrual is what payroll has to produce.

checklist.name: Ruth answered on her own terms
checklist.description: The reply grants that DEF-2211 happened the way she says and shows how this reduction differs from the one that caused it - the fact she lost is kept, and the arrangements dropped are dropped because the record cannot hold them rather than because someone judged them low risk. Scores zero if her directive is simply overridden without engaging with it.

checklist.name: Suite runs clean
checklist.description: npm test passes with the shipped three tests intact alongside whatever is added. Scores zero if the suite fails or a shipped test was removed.
